subject: Careers
title: Teamwork, boundaries and conflict
objective_verbatim: I can identify a respectful response when I disagree with someone at work.
outcomes_verbatim: I can identify a respectful response when I disagree with someone at work.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 2 Week 4, 2027-03-15 to 2027-03-19. Tuesday 16 March 2027, Tuesday P3. One 40-minute lesson. Spring 2 runs 22 February to Thursday 25 March 2027. Week 5 is four days with no Friday; the Tuesday lesson is unaffected.

outcomes_verbatim: I can identify a respectful response when I disagree with someone at work.
sources.note: The current brief supplies the exact focuses, outcomes and row mapping. Other scheme columns are not asserted verbatim. Activities and 40-minute sequencing are newly authored in the accepted Spring 1 format.
Read for file shape, timing, tiers, feedback, private response and typed/scribed access conventions.
Read for the six-outcome closing Evidence Sheet grid pattern. Current six outcomes are rows 22–27 and current Week 5 combines rows 26–27.

source_adaptation: Exact owner-supplied focus and outcomes retained. Rows 26 and 27 share the closing Week 5 lesson. Newly authored invented workplace practice, not a quotation of absent sequence/evidence columns.
timing: Read the goal. Show three safe choices: pause, speak, ask for help. Explain that all scenes are made up. Pupils do not need to share a real conflict. Allow a watch-first response. Read two replies to 'I think the boxes go here': 'You are wrong!' and 'I think they go on the shelf. Can we check?' Ask which reply helps the team and why. Make clear that people may disagree without being unkind.

Model the worked example. Pause, say a different view in a calm way, then check the task with the lead worker. Explain that respect does not mean doing something unsafe or accepting unkind words. Check for understanding: Which words state a different view without blame?

Use scenarios 1 and 2. Sort helpful and unhelpful replies. Co-write one respectful disagreement and one clear boundary. Model asking the lead worker for help. No pupil is asked to shout, threaten or play an aggressor. Use the hinge. Every pupil chooses A, B or C first. If all choose B and identify the clear limit and help route, move on. Otherwise re-model 'I cannot do that yet. Let us ask for help.' Use the parallel hinge before route work.

Offer the three tier cards. Pupils use books to choose and build respectful replies to scenes 3 and 4. Permit short spoken answers or scribing. Assess the choice and reason, not performance in roleplay.

Ask pupils to check one reply: Does it say the point? Does it avoid blame? Is help needed? Give one clear feedback point. Invite pupils to change one unhelpful phrase. Reinforce that stepping away safely and seeking help can be respectful. Read the exit scene. Accept a clear, respectful reply with checking or help. Record pupil voice, audience, support and next step on the Evidence Sheet. Offer evidence to the Communication portfolio.
timing_basis: Accepted Spring 1 Careers format: 5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40. Processing time and short pauses sit inside the total. Slides marked same task time share the 12-minute independent block.

routes.Supported: Choose a respectful reply for scene 1. Choose a clear limit for scene 3. Say or copy one reply. Point to the person who could help. Words: pause · check · space · help · lead worker Start: I think ___. Can we check? I have not been shown how. Please can you help? Please give me some space.
routes.Independent: In your book, choose a helpful reply for each scene. Write one respectful disagreement. Write one clear limit. Say when a worker should ask for help.
routes.Aspire: Complete the Independent task. Write two respectful replies for scene 4. Choose the better reply and say why. Explain why respect can include saying no.

cases.title: Scene 1
cases.situation: Two workers think the boxes go in different places.
cases.question: What could one worker say? Choose: Can we check the task? / You are silly!
cases.answer: I think they go on the shelf. Can we check the task?
cases.reason: The worker shares a view without blame and checks what to do.

cases.title: Scene 2
cases.situation: A colleague stands too close. The worker needs more space.
cases.question: What could the worker say and do?
cases.answer: Please give me some space. If it does not stop, I will ask the lead worker for help.
cases.reason: The worker states a clear limit and knows where to get help.

cases.title: Scene 3
cases.situation: A colleague asks a worker to use a tool. The worker has not been shown how.
cases.question: What is a safe, respectful reply? Choose: I have not been shown how. Let us ask for help. / I will guess.
cases.answer: I have not been shown how to use this. Let us ask the lead worker.
cases.reason: The worker can say no to an unsafe task and ask for training or help.

cases.title: Scene 4
cases.situation: One worker wants to pack first. Another wants to count first. Both speak at once.
cases.question: What could help the team?
cases.answer: Let us pause. You can speak, then I will speak. We can check the task together.
cases.reason: Taking turns helps both views be heard and gives a way to decide.

worked_example_and_fade.scene: Two workers disagree about where a box belongs.
worked_example_and_fade.model: Pause and take one slow breath if it helps. Say: 'I think the box goes on the shelf.' Ask: 'Can we check the task together?' If they still cannot agree, ask the lead worker for help.
worked_example_and_fade.thinking: I can say what I think without blame. I can ask for help if we cannot agree.
worked_example_and_fade.fade: Use the same stem for two workers who want to start different jobs: 'I think ___. Can we check ___?'
worked_example_and_fade.situation: Two workers disagree about where a box belongs.

adaptations.Cognition & Learning: Show one scene and two choices at a time. Use the same pause, speak and ask-for-help sequence. Leave a short sentence frame visible.
adaptations.Communication & Interaction: Allow a point, written reply, prepared phrase or scribe. Give thinking time. Do not judge eye contact, facial expression or volume as the outcome.
adaptations.SEMH: Use third-person invented scenes. Do not request personal accounts or acted conflict. Allow watch-first participation and a quiet pause. Praise the specific respectful choice.
adaptations.Sensory/Physical: Use paper or screen tool scenes only. Keep voices calm. Offer large print and a clear view of the response choices.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Explain disagree and boundary with simple teacher examples. Rehearse 'Can we check?' and 'Please give me space.'

ta_focus.I do: Point to the respectful words and the help route.
ta_focus.We do: Ask 'What does the worker need?' before offering a frame.
ta_focus.Independent: Give wait time. Note the pupil's choice, reason and support; do not script the whole reply.

prompt_ladder: 1 Point to the place or instruction. 2 Ask a short question. 3 Rephrase the instruction. 4 Provide a scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task.

main_hinge.question: A colleague asks a worker to use a tool they have not been shown how to use. Which reply is safe and respectful?

options.B: I have not been shown how. Let us ask the lead worker.
options.C: You are silly. Do it yourself.

main_hinge.reason: It states a clear safe limit and asks for help without blame.
main_hinge.decision: If every pupil chooses B and gives or points to the clear limit or help route, move to the route task. Otherwise model a safe limit again and use the parallel hinge.

parallel_hinge.question: A colleague keeps standing too close after a worker asks for space. What could the worker do?

options.B: Keep quiet even if they feel unsafe.
options.C: Move to a safe place and ask the lead worker for help.

parallel_hinge.reason: The worker can keep a clear boundary and seek help.

success: I can spot a respectful reply.
I can say a clear limit with kind words.
I can choose help when a problem feels unsafe.

evidence.description: Actual book/typed/pointed/oral response with date, work reference, access, supplied answers, first response, one NS and reply.

assessment: Record actual evidence against each outcome. Shown means evidence covers it with access logged. Partly means some parts shown. Not yet seen includes missing work or a pass; specify which. Do not count an adult model as independent work. Classroom practice is not proof of workplace competence.
private_help_route: Ask a trusted adult for a private talk. Point to HELP, write or use your aid. You may pass, pause and return with help. No personal story is needed.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Book, pointing, an aid, typing or an exact scribe are valid. Read back a scribed reply and allow a change. Record access apart from supplied answers. Plan in any language.

typed_route.heading: Type instead
typed_route.save: Use the usual save routine with lesson code and work reference; share privately.

feedback: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual evidence saved; R responded. R follows Voice and Audience, one NS and the pupil reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Add to Careers Portfolio. Offer to the Communication portfolio.
where_this_leads: people at work need to share views, keep safe limits and ask for help when a problem is hard to solve.
colour_blind_safe: Words and card IDs carry meaning. No colour-only codes.
accreditation: Evidence may contribute to the unit award. Staff confirm actual evidence and mapping; completion is not automatic.

Tuesday 16 March 2027 · P3 · 40 minutes · Year A
BUILD Careers · Spring 2 Week 4 · Public edition
Teamwork, boundaries and conflict
Unit: Resilience & Change — Work-ready resilience
Theme: Resilience & Change. Five teaching weeks. Week 5 is the closing lesson and brings rows 26 and 27 together. Group: up to five learners. Supported is the default.
Exact lesson outcomes
I can identify a respectful response when I disagree with someone at work.
Source: BUILD Careers scheme, Spring 2 rows 25. Focus and outcomes supplied verbatim in the current brief.
Prepare and purpose

Teach useful habits with invented, unnamed workplaces. Books, pens, Support Cards, Vocabulary Mat and Evidence Sheet. Print cards as reusable references. No write-on pupil sheets, internet, login or personal phone is needed. Read the exact outcome aloud and explain the short goal.
Where this leads: people at work need to share views, keep safe limits and ask for help when a problem is hard to solve.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So; British Values IL/MR. Respectful speech, a private choice of response and safe help-seeking are practised.
Forty minute sequence

table: Get your book. Write the date and title. Choose PAUSE, SPEAK or ASK FOR HELP. Which words help? 'You are wrong!' or 'Can we check?'
Listen: 'I think the boxes go on the shelf. Can we check the task?'
Help the group choose kind words. Practise saying, 'Please give me space.' Choose a safe, respectful reply. Give a reason, or point to the clue.
In your book, choose a route. Choose or write words that show respect and keep a clear limit.
Read one reply back. Make one small change if it would help. Two workers want to use the same space. What could one say?

blocks_in_document_order.paragraph: Teaching and checks
Arrival and retrieval 5 minutes

Read the goal. Show three safe choices: pause, speak, ask for help. Explain that all scenes are made up. Pupils do not need to share a real conflict. Allow a watch-first response. Read two replies to 'I think the boxes go here': 'You are wrong!' and 'I think they go on the shelf. Can we check?' Ask which reply helps the team and why. Make clear that people may disagree without being unkind.
I do 8 minutes

Model the worked example. Pause, say a different view in a calm way, then check the task with the lead worker. Explain that respect does not mean doing something unsafe or accepting unkind words. Check for understanding: Which words state a different view without blame?
We do 10 minutes

Use scenarios 1 and 2. Sort helpful and unhelpful replies. Co-write one respectful disagreement and one clear boundary. Model asking the lead worker for help. No pupil is asked to shout, threaten or play an aggressor. Use the hinge. Every pupil chooses A, B or C first. If all choose B and identify the clear limit and help route, move on. Otherwise re-model 'I cannot do that yet. Let us ask for help.' Use the parallel hinge before route work.
You do 12 minutes

Offer the three tier cards. Pupils use books to choose and build respectful replies to scenes 3 and 4. Permit short spoken answers or scribing. Assess the choice and reason, not performance in roleplay.
Review and exit 5 minutes

Ask pupils to check one reply: Does it say the point? Does it avoid blame? Is help needed? Give one clear feedback point. Invite pupils to change one unhelpful phrase. Reinforce that stepping away safely and seeking help can be respectful. Read the exit scene. Accept a clear, respectful reply with checking or help. Record pupil voice, audience, support and next step on the Evidence Sheet. Offer evidence to the Communication portfolio.
Model and fade
Pause and take one slow breath if it helps. Say: 'I think the box goes on the shelf.' Ask: 'Can we check the task together?' If they still cannot agree, ask the lead worker for help.

Model and card answers
All workplace cases are invented. Accept equivalent safe language. Do not require a public performance or a personal history.
Card A
I think they go on the shelf. Can we check the task?
The worker shares a view without blame and checks what to do.
Card B
Please give me some space. If it does not stop, I will ask the lead worker for help.
The worker states a clear limit and knows where to get help.
Card C
I have not been shown how to use this. Let us ask the lead worker.
The worker can say no to an unsafe task and ask for training or help.
Card D
Let us pause. You can speak, then I will speak. We can check the task together.
Taking turns helps both views be heard and gives a way to decide.
Worked example and fade
Pause and take one slow breath if it helps. Say: 'I think the box goes on the shelf.' Ask: 'Can we check the task together?' If they still cannot agree, ask the lead worker for help.
Fade only answer cues; keep reading and communication access.
Judgement and safe delivery
Main hinge

A colleague asks a worker to use a tool they have not been shown how to use. Which reply is safe and respectful? A: Fine. I will try it.  B: I have not been shown how. Let us ask the lead worker.  C: You are silly. Do it yourself. Key B. It states a clear safe limit and asks for help without blame.
Parallel hinge

A colleague keeps standing too close after a worker asks for space. What could the worker do? A: Shout an insult.  B: Keep quiet even if they feel unsafe.  C: Move to a safe place and ask the lead worker for help. Key C. The worker can keep a clear boundary and seek help.
If every pupil chooses B and gives or points to the clear limit or help route, move to the route task. Otherwise model a safe limit again and use the parallel hinge.
What to retain

Respectful response to disagreement; Boundary and safe help step. Record the actual words or selections, first attempt, work reference, usual access, supplied choices and answers, one NS and reply. Spelling and handwriting are not the target.
Common errors
Respect means saying yes to every request. A worker can say no to an unsafe task and ask for help with kind, clear words.
A disagreement must be fixed by the two workers on their own. They can pause and ask a lead worker for help, especially if a boundary is ignored or anyone feels unsafe.

Teach useful habits with invented, unnamed workplaces. Books, pens, Support Cards, Vocabulary Mat and Evidence Sheet. Print cards as reusable references. No write-on pupil sheets, internet, login or personal phone is needed. Read the exact outcome aloud and explain the short goal.

blocks_in_document_order.paragraph: Teaching and checks
Arrival and retrieval 5 minutes

Read the goal. Show three safe choices: pause, speak, ask for help. Explain that all scenes are made up. Pupils do not need to share a real conflict. Allow a watch-first response. Read two replies to 'I think the boxes go here': 'You are wrong!' and 'I think they go on the shelf. Can we check?' Ask which reply helps the team and why. Make clear that people may disagree without being unkind.
I do 8 minutes

Model the worked example. Pause, say a different view in a calm way, then check the task with the lead worker. Explain that respect does not mean doing something unsafe or accepting unkind words. Check for understanding: Which words state a different view without blame?
We do 10 minutes

Use scenarios 1 and 2. Sort helpful and unhelpful replies. Co-write one respectful disagreement and one clear boundary. Model asking the lead worker for help. No pupil is asked to shout, threaten or play an aggressor. Use the hinge. Every pupil chooses A, B or C first. If all choose B and identify the clear limit and help route, move on. Otherwise re-model 'I cannot do that yet. Let us ask for help.' Use the parallel hinge before route work.
You do 12 minutes

Offer the three tier cards. Pupils use books to choose and build respectful replies to scenes 3 and 4. Permit short spoken answers or scribing. Assess the choice and reason, not performance in roleplay.
Review and exit 5 minutes

Ask pupils to check one reply: Does it say the point? Does it avoid blame? Is help needed? Give one clear feedback point. Invite pupils to change one unhelpful phrase. Reinforce that stepping away safely and seeking help can be respectful. Read the exit scene. Accept a clear, respectful reply with checking or help.
